result.title: Forget What Comes Next: LLM Unlearning via Statistical Independence
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can memorize and reproduce fragments of their training data, raising privacy and legal concerns that motivate machine unlearning. Yet poisoned training examples can remain statistically detectable after unlearning, which raises the question of whether current unlearning objectives remove what the model has memorized at all. In this work, we introduce PINT, a novel algorithm for machine unlearning that uses the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC) to reduce the statistical dependence between tokens to be forgotten and the internal representations used to predict them. We formally relate our HSIC-based objective to Exact Memorization through a computable upper bound, connecting the training objective directly to the model's ability to reproduce the forgotten tokens. In extensive experiments, we compare forgetting-utility trade-offs across eight settings with models up to 7B parameters and demonstrate scalability to 70B parameter models. Our evaluations cover unlearning Gaussian poisons, personal information, hazardous knowledge in biology and cybersecurity, and copyrighted books and news articles. PINT achieves the strongest forgetting-utility trade-off on average and is the only method to make Gaussian poisons undetectable while maintaining near-original model utility. Code is available at: https://github.com/shkabrii/PINT

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PINT：用 Hilbert-Schmidt 独立性准则（HSIC）降低待遗忘 token 与其预测所依赖的内部表示之间的统计依赖，并给出该目标与 Exact Memorization 的可计算上界关系，在八种设定及至 70B 模型上比较遗忘—效用权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其直接在内部表示上施加独立性约束的训练目标，可能可供核查作为控制 latent 状态信息含量、抑制特定 token 依赖的正则或度量手段；但论文面向纯文本遗忘，与视觉推理无直接关联，迁移价值需自行判断。
